content.content:
That is correct behaviour at version zero, where there is no older state to skip; it is wrong
everywhere else, and adding a pack to a live repo is everywhere else.

The runner declares each pack, vendors its content, stamps it and every pack in its `requires`
closure at the newest version, runs any one-shot seed ops, and gates on the converged tree's own
self-test. It exits non-zero on a refusal or an unanswered interview — a pack already installed is
**refused**, because reinstalling would restamp the repo to the newest version while skipping every
record in between.

Then **refresh the README pack-badge row**, from the mount you just rebuilt:

```
node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs <owner/repo> --badges
```

Declaring a pack is what makes that row wrong, and adoption is the only moment anything derives it —
the nightly deliberately leaves a repo's README alone, so a row not refreshed here stays stale until
someone notices by eye. The converge rewrites the row in place between its
`<!-- claudinite:packs -->` markers, keeping whatever the repo wrote after the closing one, and is a
no-op when the row is already right. A repo that has deleted its row keeps it deleted only if you
skip this — dropping the row is a real choice, so don't re-seed one the repo removed on purpose.

## 4. Scaffold what the pack now demands

A newly active pack may require structure the repo doesn't have yet — deliberately, so the
declaration is a statement of intent that its own findings then guide you to satisfy. Run the
world sweep and let each finding name the file: e.g. `product-wiki` wants its index and the
reviewed `product-requirements/` sink before the isolation wall has anything to guard. Scaffold
per the pack's own README template; the pack's rules are the checklist.

## 4b. File what adoption cannot do

A pack may declare `adoptionHandover` — steps only a human can perform (a repository or
console setting, a permission, a secret). The install runner prints them; they are not
optional and they are not PR-body notes. **Open one tracking issue per adopting repo**,
a checkbox per step, carrying each step's `breaks` (what is broken while it is off) and
`done` (its closing condition) verbatim. Per-repo manual work reliably does not happen,
so an unfiled step is a capability that dies silently in that member.

Say on the adoption PR that the issue exists and link it. If the repo already has an
open issue for the same steps, comment there rather than opening a second.

## 5. Land

World and work checks green (`.claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`; the Stop hook
carries the work checks). Commit referencing the task's issue, push, open one PR. Content a pack
seeds through this flow — a `product-wiki` wiki's first researched, cited pages — rides the same
review gate as any other change; it is never pushed straight to the default branch.

**A failing check is your work, not the reviewer's.** Declaring a pack is what switched those rules
on, so every finding they now produce belongs to this change — fix it here, in the repo, before the
PR opens. Two things that are *not* fixes: silencing a rule by adding it to `rules`/`accept` in
`.claudinite-checks.json`, and undeclaring the pack to make the findings stop. Both turn a real
signal off on the repo's first exposure to it. If a finding genuinely cannot be satisfied — the pack
demands structure this repo has decided against — that is evidence the pack is **not** the right fit:
drop it from the declaration, say why on the PR, and let the smaller adoption land.

**Never leave the repo red.** Whatever stops you — a check you cannot satisfy, an unanswered
interview question, a scaffold that needs a decision — get the tree green first and open the PR on
what is settled. An incomplete adoption in a green repo is a handoff; an incomplete adoption in a
red one is a bug report against you.

input.title: Fleet dashboard: take the roster from live owner enumeration, not usage-fleet.GENERATED.json
input.body:
The fleet dashboard currently gets its member list from `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"` — a stored list, recomputed nightly by the `fleet-usage` task.

`claudinite-dashboard` `60821.2` (converged here today) enumerates the roster **live, as the viewer**: config `owner` plus an optional `exclude`, with archived repos and forks dropped by their own state. That is the permission-correct source — a repo the viewer cannot read simply is not in their fleet — and it is the last read of `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json`, which unblocks retiring the aggregate entirely.

Change: on the `claudinite-dashboard` entry in `.claudinite-checks.json`, replace `rosterFile` with

```json
"owner": "missingbulb",
"exclude": ["missingbulb/empty"]
```

`missingbulb/Sheepdog` needs no exclude entry — it is archived, and `inFleet` drops archived repos and forks without anyone maintaining a list. `missingbulb/empty` is neither, so it is named.

Done when: the Pages URL serves the fleet dashboard and its network log contains no request for `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json`.

Upstream plan: missingbulb/Claudinite#1158.

input.title: Fleet dashboard: enumerate the roster as the viewer
input.head: claude/fleet-roster-from-owner
input.body:
The `claudinite-dashboard` entry took its member list from `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"` — a stored list, recomputed nightly by the `fleet-usage` task. This replaces it with live enumeration:

```json
"owner": "missingbulb",
"exclude": ["missingbulb/empty"]
```

The page enumerates that owner's repos **in the browser, as the viewer**, so the fleet a person sees is exactly the fleet they can read. `missingbulb/Sheepdog` needs no entry — archived repos and forks drop out by their own state; `missingbulb/empty` is neither, so it is named.

This is the last read of `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json`, which is what unblocks retiring the aggregate (missingbulb/Claudinite#1166).

Verified by running this repo's own vendored `build-site.mjs` against the edited declaration:

```
mode: fleet-dashboard
covers: every repo under missingbulb the viewer can read, less 1 excluded
canon reference: missingbulb/Claudinite
```

`claudinite-dashboard` converged to `60821.2` here earlier today, so the `owner` key is understood by the mount this builds from.

Noticed while verifying, not fixed here: `digests` reads `not set — the morning-brief panel is off`, so this deployment does not surface the briefs it writes. Filed separately.

Closes #135. Upstream plan: missingbulb/Claudinite#1158.

input.title: The dashboard's morning-brief panel is off, on the repo that writes the briefs
input.body:
`build-site.mjs` reports, on every build here:

```
digests: not set — the morning-brief panel is off
```

`digestsRepo` and `digestsPath` are read off the `claudinite-dashboard` entry in `.claudinite-checks.json`, and this repo sets neither — so the emitted `dashboard.config.json` carries `"digestsRepo": null` and the panel never renders. Meanwhile the `fleet-digest` task runs here daily and writes into `digests/`, so the briefs are produced and nothing reads them.

Fix is one entry on that declaration:

```json
"digestsRepo": "missingbulb/Shepherd",
"digestsPath": "digests"
```

(`digestsPath` defaults to `digests` in the pack, so naming it is optional.)

Pre-existing — not introduced by #136, just surfaced by its build output. Kept out of that PR because it is a separate concern.

input.title: Adopt claudinite-dashboard — the per-repo dashboard, in repo mode
input.body:
`claudinite-dashboard` was rebuilt around a per-repo page: at-a-glance tiles, one work table with stuck/pending/all views, a 48h hourly run graph and a 30-day growth panel, all rendered from this repo's own `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` plus a handful of ETag-revalidated live reads.

Which dashboard a deployment builds is decided by its config's **shape**: a declaration naming a roster source (`owner`, or the legacy `rosterFile`) builds the fleet page, anything else builds this repo's own. This repo names none, so adopting the pack gives it the repo dashboard with nothing to configure.

Adopt it here per [adopt-pack](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-lifecycle/skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md): declare, vendor through the install runner, refresh the badge row, get the checks green, and file the pack's `adoptionHandover` steps as their own issue.

Done when: this repo's Pages URL serves the repo dashboard.

Upstream plan: missingbulb/Claudinite#1158.

input.title: claudinite-dashboard adoption: the setup steps only a human can do
input.body:
Adopting `claudinite-dashboard` (#152) brings three steps no Action can perform. Each is quoted from the pack's own `adoptionHandover`, with what breaks while it is off and what closes it.

- [ ] **Enable GitHub Pages on this repo with source "GitHub Actions"** — [Settings → Pages](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/settings/pages).
  - while off: the deploy job fails on every run; the build still succeeds, so nothing else is affected
  - done when: the Pages URL serves the dashboard, and the Claudinite dashboard workflow is green
  - *note:* missingbulb/Claudinite#1158 records this as already done ahead of the adoption. The first `Claudinite dashboard` run after #153 merges is what confirms it — if that run is green, tick this and move on.

- [ ] **Add the Actions secret `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`** — [Settings → Secrets → Actions](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/settings/secrets/actions). A fine-grained PAT on this account covering **all** repositories, granted Metadata read, Contents read, Issues read, Pull requests read.
  - while off: the daily `fleet-digest` task parks asking for the secret, so no brief is written and the dashboard's brief series has a hole for every day it is missing; the page itself still builds
  - done when: the secret exists and the next `fleet-digest` run writes a brief
  - *this one has teeth here:* the pack has no config gate for the digest task, so a repo that adopts it for the page alone gets the task too. Until the secret exists, expect a parked work item every day.

- [ ] **Decide how this dashboard authenticates its viewers** — leave it on the pasted-token box (nothing to do), or give it a Sign in button: register a GitHub App with read-only Contents, Issues and Actions, install it on the account holding these repos, deploy the pack's `oauth-exchange` example, and set `clientId` and `exchangeUrl` on this pack's declaration. See "Who has to register the app" in the pack README — one App serves every deployment you own, and none can be inherited from another owner.
  - while off: nothing fails, but a viewer who has not pasted a token reads GitHub anonymously at 60 requests/hour per IP — which one fleet sweep exceeds, so the page serves cached data or empty rows until the hour rolls
  - done when: a signed-in viewer sees the rate pill read "…/5000 · user", **or** this repo has recorded that the token box is this deployment's answer

Closes nothing on its own — this issue closes when all three boxes are ticked.

---

input.title: Adopt claudinite-dashboard
input.head: claude/adopt-claudinite-dashboard
input.body:
Turns on `claudinite-dashboard` here, in **repo mode**.

Which dashboard a deployment builds follows from its config's shape: a declaration naming a roster source (`owner`, or the legacy `rosterFile`) builds the fleet page, anything else builds this repo's own. This declaration names none, so there is nothing to configure — the mode is the shape.

Vendored through `updates/install.mjs`, not by hand, so the stamp lands at `60821.2` without burning the migration records in between. It also:

- seeds `.github/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml`,
- wires `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` into the executor's secret block, for the `fleet-digest` task the pack brings with it,
- adds the pack's badge to the README row.

`check_the_world.mjs` is green on this branch. Verified it is actually running rather than silently passing, by declaring a bogus pack id and watching it go blocking, then restoring.

The install runner printed three `adoptionHandover` steps only a human can do — Pages, the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret, and the viewer-auth decision. They are filed with their `breaks`/`done` conditions in #153, not left as notes here.

One thing worth knowing before merge: the install ended `needs-human` on two **pre-existing** unanswered interview questions — `barriers/goals` and `claude-code-web-users-support/store` — neither of which belongs to this adoption. They were already unanswered on this declaration before today; the vendoring, stamping and seeding all completed. Left alone rather than answered on the owner's behalf.

Refs #152.

* Republish the dashboard when the mount moves, not only on a human push

The published site is stuck on claudinite-dashboard v10 while main's mount
carries v12, so the fleet grid still shows the "mount has not converged in
N days" verdict v11 removed. Nothing is wrong with the page: the deploy
never fires. Claudinite's update PRs are auto-merged by github-actions[bot],
and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow, so every converge
lands without a build.

The catch-up follows the vendored scheduler, which is this repo's one
permitted cron, and asks on each of its wake-ups whether the page's sources
have moved since the last successful deploy — so the hourly cadence costs a
cache lookup rather than an hourly republish of identical bytes.

* Hash every generated artifact, not the roster by name

The already-deployed gate hashed `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` because that
is what this deployment's roster happens to be called — but the roster's
file name is per-deployment config, and a member list that changed under a
different name would leave the site serving the old one. The glob is
over-inclusive by design: an extra rebuild costs one run, a missed one
costs a stale page.

Keeps this file identical to the pack's stub below its header.

#!/bin/bash
# The fold lands a commit on each member's default branch, so "main moved past the sha
# it held right after the forced converge" IS that member having folded (or done other
# work) since. Only the repos this session can read anonymously are watchable; the
# private ones are answered later by the fleet census.
REPOS="Claudinite ClaudiniteCanary ClaudiniteWebsite CrosswordChat EdFringeNow GoogleCalendarEventCreator LaughCounter MissingBulbWebsite Shepherd ShoutsAndWhispers TLDR VascularColoring WIP"
declare -A BASE
VISIBLE=0
for r in $REPOS; do
  s=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/missingbulb/$r refs/heads/main 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
  [ -n "$s" ] && { BASE[$r]=$s; VISIBLE=$((VISIBLE+1)); }
done
echo "watching $VISIBLE of $(echo $REPOS | wc -w) members (rest are private)"
DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + 3300 ))
while :; do
  MOVED=0; STILL=""
  for r in "${!BASE[@]}"; do
    s=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/missingbulb/$r refs/heads/main 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
    if [ -n "$s" ] && [ "$s" != "${BASE[$r]}" ]; then MOVED=$((MOVED+1)); else STILL="$STILL $r"; fi
  done
  echo "$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) moved=$MOVED/$VISIBLE still:$STILL"
  [ "$MOVED" -ge "$VISIBLE" ] && { echo "ALL VISIBLE MOVED"; exit 0; }
  [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$DEADLINE" ] && { echo "DEADLINE moved=$MOVED/$VISIBLE still:$STILL"; exit 1; }
  sleep 90
done
EOF

Tracking issue for the dashboard redesign. The plan below is ordered by what blocks (out-of-band setup → one review pass over a PR stack → unattended execution → destructive tail), not by subject. Once agreed, this body is append-only.

## First, the question asked: is `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` redundant?

**Yes — with one catch that sequences the removal.**

- The sweep is a **stateless full recompute, a pure function of the members' current files** (its own README says so). It holds **no longer history** than the members: each member's week rows are append-once and never pruned, so the member files are the complete record and the fleet file adds no depth.
- **Nothing in the canon reads it.** Grep finds only the task's own files, its tests, docs and the `.gitattributes` entry. It was built for fleet-wide analysis by a human/agent reading one file — the fleet dashboard is now that reader, better.
- The **access argument is real and favors dropping**: the aggregate in Shepherd shows anyone with Shepherd read the whole fleet's numbers, while the dashboard reads each member's file *as the viewer* — a repo you can't read renders "not visible to you". Per-repo files are the permission-correct source.
- **Catch 1 — it is currently the fleet dashboard's roster.** Shepherd's declaration reads `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"`. The member list is the one thing genuinely fleet-shaped in it, so the fleet page needs a replacement roster source *before* the file goes (PR 3 below).
- Catch 2 — the `coverage` census (absent / dormant / out-of-scope, with reasons) is the only other content member files can't hold. The fleet page derives it live: a rostered repo with no readable usage file **is** the absent row, and `dormant` is read off the member's own declaration.

So: drop the task and the file — sequenced after the fleet page stops reading it (the tail, below).

## Design decisions

1. **Fresh vs past split.** *Fresh* per page load: repo metadata, head sha, the open-issue page, the runs list — all ETag-revalidated (a 304 is free), target **~5 requests warm, all 304s** on the per-repo page. *Past*: one blob read of `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`, cached by head sha — **zero requests while `main` is unmoved**. Nothing else reaches back in time over the API.
2. **usage.GENERATED.json v3 stays raw data**, not UI-shaped: per-hour and per-day series with per-item detail preserved, so future UI changes re-render without re-folding. Readers accept v2 (legacy at the door): an absent series renders as a stated gap, never a guessed zero — the #1001 rule.
3. **Freshness provenance**: a `generated` stamp in the file, excluded from the worker's unchanged-compare exactly as the fleet file's `generatedAt` already is — so it reads "when the data last moved" and a quiet repo still opens no PR. The head-commit date the page already holds is the upper bound beside it.
4. **usage-fold goes hourly, gated on movement** — signals `commits` + `conversationLogs` + runs movement; a quiet hour declines. The REST-read families stay incremental past their watermarks; day recomputes stay local-git and free.
5. **Mode is structural, no new config key**: a declaration with a roster source (`owner` or legacy `rosterFile`) is a **fleet-dashboard** deployment, anything else is a **repo-dashboard** one; `build-site.mjs` mounts that landing. Nothing to ask at adoption, nothing to misconfigure.
6. **Fleet roster = live enumeration as the viewer**: config `owner` (+ existing `exclude`), membership = a readable `.claudinite-checks.json` at head (sha-cached, so the probe is amortized). This also honors the standing "no repo list exists anywhere in canon code" decision. Fallback if enumeration proves too costly at fleet size: a slim `roster.GENERATED.json` from a Shepherd fleet task (the sanctioned daily auto-merged GENERATED-file shape) — not built unless measurement says so.

## Phase 0 — out-of-band, human

- [x] Enable **Pages, source "GitHub Actions", on ClaudiniteCanary** — the one repository setting no Action can flip. The adoption run files its own handover issue there with the link; while off, only the deploy job fails. (Shepherd already deploys, so its setting is expected on — verified as an execution step, promoted here only if it turns out off.)

Sign-in for the fleet deployment is already tracked in #996 / #942 / #1003 and blocks nothing here — the token box works today.

## The stack — all code, one review pass, merged base-first

- [x] **PR 1 — usage-fold v3** (the data plane; everything downstream renders from it)
  - **`hours` tier**, rolling ~72h keyed by UTC hour: counts of scheduler runs / executor runs / agentic runs, plus raw per-run entries (task ids evaluated / executed, which dispatched an agent, conclusion) so the UI can build hover detail. Folded from the Actions runs listing + the run records, incremental past `runsFoldedThrough`. This is the queue-era successor to the dead `tasks` census — closes #994.
  - **day-row additions**: `queue` — closed work items per task × outcome, appended past a watermark (settled data, never re-read); `ruleTokens` — sessions seen + rule tokens summed, parsed from the session-start summary line the capture logs already carry; `linesCommitted` — local git, free; `releases` — tags, one cheap read.
  - **aspirational, resolved inside this PR**: per-session token spend — probe the capture JSONL for usage records; carried if present, otherwise the README names it absent (a stated gap, not an approximation).
  - `generated` stamp per decision 3; `frequency: 'hourly'` + movement precondition per decision 4; README rewritten.
  - Exit: fold runs green on this repo's own logs; a v2 file re-folds to v3 without loss; a quiet-hour run declines.
- [x] **PR 2 — per-repo page redesign**
  - **At-a-glance tiles**: stars, CI health, waiting-on-a-person minutes (the fleet's flat-rate constant, same published assumption note), "N parked for approval / M for a decision" (the park-kind split `summariseMember` already makes, reused per-repo), open PRs + issues, engine/pack drift vs `canonRepo` (reads *unknown* when unset — never guessed).
  - **One work table** replacing the tasks and queue tables: three views — **stuck / pending / all** — over the union of declared tasks and their items, with view-dependent columns; transitions FLIP-animated (rows enter/leave, columns slide; hand-rolled, the pack keeps zero dependencies). Blocked/parked rows always on top; healthy rows collapsed behind **show all**.
  - **Task execution summary**: per-day stacked outcome bars (the fleet's shape), from the usage `queue` series, today's partial day topped up from the live issue page already fetched.
  - **Scheduler-runs panel condensed to a 48h hourly stacked graph** — scheduler / executor / agentic per hour, hover naming the tasks evaluated / executed / agentic — from the usage `hours` tier, the freshest hours topped up from the runs list already fetched.
  - **Growth block, centrally placed**: 30-day graph, dual axes — rule tokens added to sessions per day, checks executed per day — plus the aspirational series where the file carries them.
  - Exit: cold/warm request counts measured and stated in the README, warm within the ~5-request target.
- [x] **PR 3 — fleet page from member usage files**
  - Member rows and the activity/growth panels render from each member's usage file (sha-keyed read, zero when unmoved) plus a minimal fresh read per member (ETag'd open-issue page + repo meta), through the existing cache/budget tiers.
  - Roster from `owner` enumeration per decision 6; `rosterFile` still accepted so Shepherd's current declaration keeps working until flipped.
  - A rostered member with no usage file renders **"not folding yet"** — the coverage census, absorbed.
  - Exit: fleet page renders against Shepherd's fleet with `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` unread (network log clean of it when `owner` is configured).
- [x] **PR 4 — modes + docs**
  - `build-site.mjs` mounts the repo- or fleet-landing per decision 5.
  - README rewrites: claudinite-dashboard (panels, modes, data plane, measured budgets); `docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md` updated to the end state (per-repo files are the record, the dashboard is the fleet reader; the fleet aggregate gone). The sheepdog README row goes with the tail's removal PR, not here.

## Execution — runnable in one sitting, no waits

- [ ] Force **usage-fold fleet-wide** (fleet-baseline `follow`, or the scheduler's `wake` per member) so every member's file regenerates at v3 in one pass rather than trickling in over nightly cycles. Exit: every folding member's file reads `version: 3`. (Readers accept v2, so a straggler costs nothing meanwhile.)
- [x] **Adopt claudinite-dashboard on ClaudiniteCanary** via adopt-pack (no roster → repo mode by shape). Exit: Canary's Pages URL serves the repo dashboard.
- [x] **Flip Shepherd's declaration**: replace `"rosterFile": "usage-fleet.GENERATED.json"` with `"owner": "missingbulb"` beside its existing excludes. Exit: Shepherd's Pages URL serves the fleet dashboard with no request for `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json`.
- [x] Verify Shepherd's Pages setting was indeed already on (expected no-op).

## The tail — destructive, only after the cutover is observed working

- [x] File (do-later, blocked behind PR 3's merge **and** the Shepherd flip) the removal: the `fleet-usage` task, `aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs`, its README + the sheepdog catalog row + the `.gitattributes` entry from the canon; `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` deleted from Shepherd. Filed as work that comes back on its own, never a phase recalled from memory.

## Not in this plan

- Sign-in / GitHub App wiring — #996, #942, #1003.
- Any pre-summed fleet artifact — decision 6's fallback exists only if enumeration measurement forces it.

## Execution run — 2026-08-21

Boxes above updated to match. Three of the four execution steps are done and verified; the fourth is in flight and is the only thing left in this plan.

### The fleet update, first

Forcing `usage-fold` before the fleet held the new pack would just have run the old fold, so the update went first — a `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-baseline` item on Shepherd (missingbulb/Shepherd#132), which converged `task:done` in 38 seconds:

```
| fired | skipped | failed |
|  13   |    6    |   0    |
```

Skipped, each named rather than silently dropped: canon (self-skips), three self-declared dormant members, `missingbulb/empty` (excluded), `missingbulb/Sheepdog` (archived).

### Force usage-fold fleet-wide — in flight, not yet ticked

The converge is itself the trigger: it lands a commit on each member's default branch, which is exactly what `usage-fold`'s movement precondition gates on, so every member that converged folds at its next hourly anchor without needing a second lever.

**Proven in production on Shepherd** — forced there directly and watched the file turn over:

```
version: 3
generated: 2026-08-21T15:13:58.004Z
top keys: version, generated, foldedThrough, runsFoldedThrough, queueFoldedThrough, fields, hours, days, weeks
hours tier: 22 entries
day fields: captures, merges, sessions, userMessages, userCommands, ruleTokens,
            ruleTokenSessions, tokensIn, tokensOut, tokenSessions, commits,
            linesAdded, linesRemoved, releases
```

The stated exit is *every* folding member at `version: 3`, and that is still converging across the other 12. Left unticked until the census says so rather than ticked on one member's evidence.

**Departure from the plan worth recording:** there is no lever that forces an arbitrary task fleet-wide. `fleet-baseline` hard-codes `FORCED_TASK = 'update'`, and the alternative the plan names — the scheduler's `wake` per member — needs Actions-write on each member, which a session scoped to a few repos does not have. It cost nothing here because the converge triggers the fold anyway, but the gap is real and is filed separately.

### Adopt claudinite-dashboard on ClaudiniteCanary — done

input.title: fleet-baseline can only force `update` — there is no lever for any other task fleet-wide
input.body:
`fleet-baseline` is the fleet's only forcing lever, and it hard-codes what it forces:

```js
// packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs
export const FORCED_TASK = 'update';
```

Everything underneath it is already generic — `fireScheduler(gh, fullName, ref, taskId)` takes the id as an argument, and the member-side `planWake` accepts a whitespace/comma-separated list of `task` or `pack/task` ids and *creates* the standing item when one is missing. Only the constant is fixed.

So "force task X across the fleet" has exactly one route today: dispatch each member's `claudinite-scheduler.yml` yourself with `wake: X`. That needs Actions-write on every member, which is the credential `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` exists to hold and which an interactive session scoped to a handful of repos does not have. The alternative — attaching every member to the session — is per-repo manual work, which reliably does not happen.

Surfaced doing #1158's "force `usage-fold` fleet-wide" step. It cost nothing there: the converge `fleet-baseline` forces lands a commit on each member's default branch, and that commit is exactly what `usage-fold`'s movement precondition gates on, so forcing `update` forced the fold one hop later by accident. The next task that wants a fleet-wide force will not be so lucky.

**Shape of the fix** (the lever's `README` already documents the parameter-bag pattern this would join): a `WAKE` context parameter beside the existing `REPOS` / `DRY_RUN` / `INCLUDE_DORMANT`, defaulting to `update` so every existing item keeps its meaning, passed through to `fireScheduler` and named in the run summary. The summary line already reads *"Asked each covered member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` to wake its `update` item"* — it would just stop being a constant.

Two things to get right, both learned the hard way in this repo:

- **The protocol spans repos.** The dispatch input is read by each member's own vendored scheduler stub, so a new spelling has to be one every fielded stub already understands. `wake` itself is unchanged here — only which id travels in it — so this should be safe, but it is the class of change that broke Shepherd's only caller in #929.
- **A parameter that stops being read must fail loudly** (#974). If `WAKE` is added, an item naming a task no declared pack owns must land in the summary's `failed` list, not dispatch `update` silently because the name did not resolve.

Not urgent — nothing is blocked on it — but it is a hole in the fleet's control surface that is invisible until someone needs it.

input.title: Record what a vendored engine script's 401 means in a session — GITHUB_TOKEN is `[REDACTED:env:GH_TOKEN]`
input.body:
Running a vendored engine script from a session shell — `create-work-item.mjs`, and by construction every other script that calls `makeGh()` — fails with a **401 Bad credentials** on every call. The cause is not the script and not the grant:

```
$ env | grep GITHUB_TOKEN
GITHUB_TOKEN=[REDACTED:env:GH_TOKEN]
```

The real credential lives in the agent proxy, which swaps it in for requests that go *through* it. `curl` picks the proxy up from `HTTPS_PROXY` and gets the swap; **Node's `fetch` ignores `HTTPS_PROXY` by default**, connects direct, and sends the literal string `[REDACTED:env:GH_TOKEN]` — hence 401, not 403.

`NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` makes Node 22+ honour the proxy env, and the same call then reaches GitHub:

```
$ NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node -e "fetch('https://api.github.com/user',{headers:{authorization:'Bearer '+process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN}}).then(r=>console.log(r.status))"
200
```

That is worth recording because **401 and 403 are different diagnoses here and the fix for one is not the fix for the other**:

- **401** — the process is not going through the proxy. Fixable: `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`.
- **403 `"GitHub access is not enabled for this session"`** — the proxy reached GitHub and refused. Not fixable from the shell. Every `/repos/...` endpoint returns this, read or write, in-scope repo or not; only `/user` succeeds. The existing rule about `api.github.com` being unusable from the shell is correct, and this run re-confirmed it endpoint by endpoint.

So the sequence a session actually hits is: 401 (looks like a broken grant) → set the flag → 403 (the real, unfixable answer) → use the MCP tools. Two dead ends that look like one, and the first one looks like the script's fault.

This is #1133's class from the other side — that issue recorded that scripts written for an Actions context 401 in a session; this records *why*, and that clearing the 401 does not get you a working script.

Practical consequence for pure-computation helpers: the vendored code is still usable in a session for anything that does not touch the network. Generating a work item's exact title and body with the repo's own `work-item.mjs` and then posting it through `mcp__github__issue_write` produces the same artifact the CLI would have — which is how missingbulb/Shepherd#132 was created after `create-work-item.mjs` 403'd.

Refs #1158.

#!/bin/bash
# Claudinite, Shepherd and ClaudiniteCanary have already folded, so a further move is
# not their signal — they are out. For the rest, nothing else is running in them right
# now, so main moving IS the fold landing. Bounded: the authoritative per-member answer
# comes from the fleet census afterwards, this only decides when it is worth asking.
REPOS="ClaudiniteWebsite CrosswordChat EdFringeNow GoogleCalendarEventCreator LaughCounter MissingBulbWebsite ShoutsAndWhispers TLDR VascularColoring"
declare -A BASE
for r in $REPOS; do
  s=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/missingbulb/$r refs/heads/main 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
  [ -n "$s" ] && BASE[$r]=$s
done
N=${#BASE[@]}
echo "watching $N members that have not folded yet"
DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + 2700 ))
while :; do
  MOVED=0; STILL=""
  for r in "${!BASE[@]}"; do
    s=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/missingbulb/$r refs/heads/main 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
    if [ -n "$s" ] && [ "$s" != "${BASE[$r]}" ]; then MOVED=$((MOVED+1)); else STILL="$STILL $r"; fi
  done
  echo "$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) folded=$MOVED/$N still:$STILL"
  [ "$MOVED" -ge "$N" ] && { echo "ALL FOLDED"; exit 0; }
  [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$DEADLINE" ] && { echo "DEADLINE folded=$MOVED/$N still:$STILL"; exit 1; }
  sleep 120
done

input.body:
**Live, and it passes on all four.**

`In-production-when` is satisfied: `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` on `main` (at `fb7fdac`, "Claudinite: fold usage metrics (#1173)") reads `version: 3`. The fold that wrote it was executor run [32496649719](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32496649719), off work item #1172, `task:done`.

**1 — version and stamp.**
```
version: 3
generated: 2026-08-21T15:16:40.385Z   (Date.parse → valid)
```

**2 — the run listings were read.** 36 hour rows, 11 of them with a non-zero `scheduler` count. Example:
```
2026-08-21T05  {"scheduler":1,"executor":1,"agentic":0,"failed":0}
```

**3 — local git was readable.** One day row carries `commits`, and it is the only one that could:
```
2026-08-21  commits=1  linesAdded=103443  linesRemoved=0
```
The Actions checkout is depth-1, and the fold said so itself rather than leaving it to be inferred — from the run log:
```
usage-fold [#1172]: this checkout's history starts at 2026-08-21 — days before it carry no commit or line counts
```
So `coveredFrom` is today, today is the one day inside coverage, and today has the counts. The shallow probe and the `--numstat` parse both worked; this is the deliberate branch, not the `commits === null` one (whose message — "the local git history could not be read" — does not appear).

**4 — absence stayed absent.** No day lacking `commits` carries a `linesAdded`/`linesRemoved` value. Every pre-coverage day is null across all three together:
```
2026-07-23  [null, null, null]
2026-07-24  [null, null, null]
```
And note `linesRemoved: 0` on 2026-08-21 — a **real** zero sitting beside a real `commits` value, which is exactly the distinction the file shape exists to keep.

*A correction on my own working, since it nearly produced a false negative:* my first pass read `days[date]` as the totals tuple and concluded no day carried `commits` at all. Each day is an object whose tuple is under `totals`; indexing the object gave `undefined` for every field, which is indistinguishable from "no key" unless you look. The assertion passes; my first reading of it did not.

**Ungated figure — how often the hourly task opens a PR.** Two `fold` PRs merged on `main` in the preceding 24 hours:

```
fb7fdac  08-21 15:18  Claudinite: fold usage metrics (#1173)
df3ae09  08-21 04:27  Claudinite: fold skill-usage metrics (#1148)
```

Well short of the 24 that would mean the precondition or the stamp-stripped compare is not doing its job — but the number cannot carry much weight yet: the task only became hourly when #1165 merged at 14:34 today, so `#1148` is a run of the *daily* task and only ~45 minutes of hourly cadence have elapsed. One PR in that window. Worth re-reading in a day. (The 24h window is fully covered — this shallow checkout reaches back to 08-19 14:24.)

Closing as completed.

input.title: The dashboard's drift tile reads "unknown" here — canonRepo is unset
input.body:
Every build since the adoption (#154) reports:

```
canon reference: not set — member mount freshness reads unknown
```

`canonRepo` is read off the `claudinite-dashboard` entry in `.claudinite-checks.json`, and this declaration does not set it, so the page's engine/pack-drift tile has nothing to measure against and states *unknown* rather than guessing — correct behaviour, wrong configuration.

It matters more here than in most members: this repo exists to be the canon's live canary, so "how far behind canon is this mount" is the one number it should never be blind to.

Fix, on that entry:

```json
"canonRepo": "missingbulb/Claudinite"
```

The pack asks no adoption question that would have prompted this (`questions: []`), which is why the adoption did not catch it — the key simply defaults to unset.

Follow-up to #152.

- canon reference: not set — member mount freshness reads unknown
+ canon reference: missingbulb/Claudinite
```

`mode: repo-dashboard` is unchanged — `canonRepo` is not a roster source, so it does not touch which dashboard this builds.

content.text:
Answering the question directly first: **yes — Canary is entirely on the default, and it could not be anything else.**

- **Shepherd** asserts its mode: `owner: "missingbulb"` is a positive statement that this covers a fleet.
- **Canary's** declaration is the bare string `"claudinite-dashboard"` — no config object at all. It gets repo mode by saying nothing.

And the deeper part: the pack recognises eleven config keys — `clientId, exchangeUrl, redirectUri, scope, rosterUrl, repos, owner, exclude, defaultRepo, digestsRepo, digestsPath` — and **none of them can say "this is a single-repo dashboard."** Repo mode is only ever the `else` branch:

```js
isFleetConfig = (c) => Boolean(c?.owner || c?.rosterUrl || (c?.repos?.length ?? 0) > 1);
const fleetMode = Boolean(repos.length || rosterUrl || cfg.owner);
```

So I could not have "set Canary to single-repo mode" — there is nothing to set. That is decision 5's *"anything else is a repo-dashboard one"* working exactly as written, and it collides with the standing decision *avoid a default; require the value explicitly*. Nobody caught the conflict when decision 5 was agreed, me included.

It is not merely untidy. The pack's own code already names the hazard, and only warns about it:

```js
// A roster the member named but this cannot read is worth saying out loud: the
// site would otherwise publish as a single-repo dashboard and look intentional.
```

A fleet deployment that loses its roster — unreadable file, dropped key, a typo in `owner` — degrades silently into a repo dashboard that looks deliberate. Silence means repo mode, so nothing can tell "I meant one repo" from "my fleet config didn't arrive."

How to remove the default is your call, since it amends decision 5:

questions.question: How should claudinite-dashboard's mode stop being a default?

options.label: Require it explicitly (Recommended)
options.description: A `mode: "repo" | "fleet"` key on the declaration, with no default: the build FAILS when it is absent or disagrees with the config (mode: fleet and no roster source, or mode: repo beside an owner). Both members then state their mode, and a fleet deployment whose roster went missing goes red instead of quietly serving one repo. Amends decision 5's "no new config key" in #1158 — which is the part that produced the default.

options.label: Only repo mode must be asserted
options.description: Keep fleet inferred from the roster source (a deployment naming an owner plainly means a fleet), but require `mode: "repo"` to assert the single-repo case; the build fails when neither is present. Smaller change, keeps decision 5's inference intact — but leaves two ways to say "fleet", which is the shape that drifts.

options.label: Derive it from the repo, no key
options.description: Keep zero new config: a deployment is a fleet one iff the repo also declares claudinite-fleet-sheepdog (the fleet enforcer), otherwise it is its own page. Genuinely structural rather than a default — but it makes claudinite-dashboard read another pack's declaration, which is the coupling between sibling packs the standing decision warns against.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: claudinite-dashboard: a deployment states its mode, rather than repo mode being what silence means
input.body:
Raised by the owner on Canary's declaration: *"You were supposed to set claudinite-dashboard to a single-repo mode on canary and fleet mode on Shepherd. Is any of them default? It shouldn't be."*

Yes — Canary was. Its declaration was a bare `"claudinite-dashboard"` with no config, and repo mode is what saying nothing produced. Shepherd's was explicit only by accident: it names an `owner`, and naming an owner *implied* fleet.

`#1158`'s decision 5 chose that shape deliberately — *"Mode is structural, no new config key: a declaration with a roster source is a fleet-dashboard deployment, anything else is a repo-dashboard one"*. But "anything else" is a default, not a structural derivation, and it collides with the standing decision to *avoid a default; require the value explicitly*.

It is not a cosmetic distinction. The inference cannot tell **"this repo only"** from **"the fleet, whose roster source went missing"** — a dropped key, a renamed artifact, an enumeration never configured. Both present as "no roster", and the second publishes a one-repo dashboard that looks entirely intentional. The pack already half-knew this: `build-site.mjs` carried a `WARNING: rosterFile … could not be read — the site will cover only this repo`, whose own comment says the site "would otherwise publish as a single-repo dashboard and look intentional". A warning in a build log is not a guard.

## The change

`mode` becomes the pack's one required config key, with no default:

- `resolveMode(config)` in [`config.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-dashboard/config.mjs) is the single judgment, so the build and the page cannot drift into two matching-looking expressions that disagree at one input. It refuses an absent mode, a mode outside the vocabulary, and — the one worth having — a mode that **contradicts** the config: `fleet` naming no roster source, `repo` naming one.
- `isFleetConfig` reads the stated mode instead of inferring it from which other keys happen to be present.
- `build-site.mjs` exits non-zero rather than publishing a guess, and writes the mode into the config the page reads.
- The pack asks it at adoption — its only question, because it is the only fork here that has no answer right for nearly every project. Both answers are ordinary and guessing wrong publishes a plausible site covering the wrong thing.

Both existing deployments state it in the same pass — Shepherd `"fleet"`, Canary `"repo"` — so nothing is left inferring. Only those two declare the pack (checked across all 13 folding members), which is also why this needs no migration record: there is no third member for one to reach.

Closes the ambiguity decision 5 introduced; that decision is amended on #1158.

input.title: The dashboard deployment states that it is the fleet one
input.body:
Part of missingbulb/Claudinite#1179, with the pack-side change in missingbulb/Claudinite#1182.

This deployment's fleet mode was **inferred** — it names an `owner`, and naming an owner used to imply the fleet overview. That inference cannot tell a fleet whose roster source went missing from a repo that never had one, so `claudinite-dashboard` now requires the mode to be stated and the build refuses to publish without it.

One key added, `"mode": "fleet"`, beside the `owner` it already names. Nothing else changes: this was already the fleet dashboard and still is.

**Merge order.** Harmless before the pack change lands — the current build ignores an unknown key — and required after it, so this can go first or together, but should not be left behind.

Recording the amended decision on the tracking issue:

input.body:
**Decision 5 is amended.** It read:

> **Mode is structural, no new config key**: a declaration with a roster source (`owner` or legacy `rosterFile`) is a **fleet-dashboard** deployment, anything else is a **repo-dashboard** one … Nothing to ask at adoption, nothing to misconfigure.

"Anything else" is a default, not a structural derivation — and it collides with the standing decision to *avoid a default; require the value explicitly*. The owner caught it on Canary's declaration, which was a bare `"claudinite-dashboard"`: repo mode was what saying nothing produced.

The failure it allows is specific. The inference cannot tell **"this repo only"** from **"the fleet, whose roster source went missing"** — a dropped key, a renamed artifact, an enumeration never configured. Both present as "no roster", and the second publishes a one-repo dashboard that looks intentional. `build-site.mjs` already warned about exactly this shape without being able to stop it.

Amended to: **a deployment states its mode.** `mode` is `"repo"` or `"fleet"`, required, no default; the build refuses an absent mode and a mode that contradicts the config in either direction. It costs the one adoption question decision 5 was avoiding, which is the right price — both answers are ordinary, neither is rarer, and there is no value here that is right for nearly every project.

Tracked in #1179, pack change in #1182, and the two live deployments state their mode in Shepherd#142 (`fleet`) and ClaudiniteCanary#160 (`repo`).

content.text:
Here's the handover prompt.

```text
──────────────────────── PROMPT FOR A NEW SESSION ─────────────────────────
DISCLAIMER: Claude wrote this prompt. Examine it for inconsistencies and
verify its claims yourself — do not follow it blindly. Every fact below was
read off git, not the GitHub API, and the API may say something different.
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Investigate why five Claudinite members stopped converging around 10 August
2026 and have not landed a mount update since, despite running the converge
successfully every day.

## The affected members

missingbulb/CrosswordChat, missingbulb/EdFringeNow,
missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator, missingbulb/LaughCounter,
missingbulb/TLDR

## Evidence gathered (read from git only — no API access to these repos yet)

For all five, from `.claudinite-checks.json` at HEAD:

  maintenance.delivery   auto-merge            (nothing waits on a human)
  claudinite.ref         631a067f              IDENTICAL across all five
  claudinite.updated     2026-08-10 .. 08-12
  packVersions           no `claudinite-growth` key at all
                         (LaughCounter still shows the pre-date-anchored "7")

And from the remotes:

  last commit on main    2026-08-21   — the repos are live
  newest update branch   claudinite/update-2026-08-21-*  — created TODAY
  open claudinite/*      3, 8, 10, 17 and 51 branches respectively

So the scheduler runs, the converge runs, it produces an update branch every
day, and the branch never merges. The open-branch count is one per attempt,
accumulating since roughly 10 August. The identical pinned ref across all
five is the strongest signal: they all stopped advancing at the same canon
ref at the same time.

Two members on the same fleet — missingbulb/VascularColoring and
missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers — DID converge today and are at the current
pack versions, so this is a subset, not the whole fleet. Working out what
separates the five from those two is probably the fastest route to the cause.

Three more members (ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite, WIP) could not be
read at all from this session and are unknown, not healthy — check them too.

## Why it matters

It blocks the last open box on missingbulb/Claudinite#1158: every folding
member's usage file should read `"version": 3`. These five still read v2
because they never received the claudinite-growth pack version that folds v3.
Readers accept v2, so nothing is broken for a user — but the members are ~10
days behind on everything the canon has shipped, not just this.

## How to proceed

1. Attach the five repos to the session (`add_repo`, access "push"), then
   read, for each: the open `claudinite/update-*` PRs, and the head sha's
   `pull_request` check runs.
2. There is a standing rule in the canon that applies directly here:
   "Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land — `unstable` beside
   a green sweep is a parked `action_required` run, not a missing repo
   setting. Read the member's raw .claudinite-checks.json and the head sha's
   pull_request runs; propose a platform-settings change only as a
   conclusion, never as a diagnosis." Do not open with a settings theory.
3. A likely-looking hypothesis worth testing early, but NOT assuming: a
   branch-protection or Actions-permissions change around 10 August that
   auto-merge cannot satisfy. Confirm it against a real run before saying it.
4. Whatever the cause, the backlog of up to 51 stale update branches per repo
   needs a cleanup plan — but assess branches read-only and act only on
   issues, per the tidy-repo policy.

## Useful mechanics discovered this session

- `api.github.com` IS reachable from the shell with an Authorization header
  when the proxy is injecting a credential, but the injection can be lost on
  a container restart (`GITHUB_TOKEN` reads literally as "[REDACTED:env:GH_TOKEN]",
  and requests come back 401/403). Check with:
      curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user
  If that is not 200, use the GitHub MCP tools instead.
- The git proxy serves PUBLIC repos with no attachment at all, and is much
  cheaper than the MCP file reads (which return whole files). To read one
  file from many repos:
      git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --no-checkout -q \
        https://github.com/missingbulb/<REPO> <REPO>
      git -C <REPO> show HEAD:.claudinite-checks.json
  Private repos fail this and do need attaching.
- Node's `fetch` does not honour HTTPS_PROXY by default, so the vendored
  engine scripts 401 when run from a session. `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node …`
  fixes it (Node 22 — the EnvHttpProxyAgent warning is expected).

## Deliverable

A root cause named with the evidence for it, and either the fix applied or a
tracking issue in missingbulb/Claudinite stating what a human must change and
where. Link it back to #1158.
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

Meanwhile, what landed here:

| | |
|---|---|
| **`packs/claudinite-dashboard/`** | `mode` is now the pack's one required config key. `resolveMode` in `config.mjs` is the single judgment the build and page share — refusing an absent mode, an unknown one, and a mode that contradicts the config either way. `build-site.mjs` exits non-zero rather than publishing a guess. `pack.mjs` → `60821.3` with its first adoption question. |

Three PRs, all open: [#1182](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1182) (the pack), [Shepherd#142](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/142) (`"mode": "fleet"`), [ClaudiniteCanary#160](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/160) (`"mode": "repo"`). ---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
